In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 2$^{+}_{1}$ state is a three-body resonance, and that the three-body wave function is dominated by a 2$\alpha$ core and a valence $\alpha$, which has a large probability of being in a relative p-wave.
the 16.1 MeV state in C-12 has a significant component of a two alpha cluster structure, but it is not a pure alpha-alpha-core cluster state, as was claimed in previous studies.
the $ (2^{+})$ state at 16.11 MeV in 12 C decays predominantly to the 2+ state in 8 B, with an additional contribution of 5.1 (5) % to the ground state in 8 Be.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the $ (J^\pi, T) = ( 2^{+}, 1)$ state in 12 C at 16.11  MeV is a well-defined three- $\alpha$ -particle resonance with an energy width of 0.5 MeV and an $\alpha$ -$\alpha$ interaction radius of about 2.8 fm.
the $ 2^{+}$ state at 16.11MeV in 12 C is not an isobaric analog state of the 2+ ground state in 12 N, but rather a state with a large 2+ component.

we have been able to extract the branching ratios for the 16.1 MeV state in $^{12}$C to the ground and excited states in $^{8}$Be with unprecedented precision, and we have also been able to extract a complete set of the decay amplitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decay to the 2.43 MeV state in $^8$Be is dominated by d-wave, while the decay into the ground state is mostly s-wave.

the $ (2^{+})$ state in 12 C is not the only state which can decay into 8Be(2+)+$\alpha$. The 16.11-MeV state is also found to decay into the 0+ ground state of 12C and the first excited state of 8 Be with a relative branching ratio of 1.5(2).
